entities.summary:
Zhengzhou is the capital and largest city of Henan province in central China, with a population of over 12 million. Located in the Central Plains at the intersection of the Yellow River and the ancient Silk Road east-west routes, Zhengzhou is one of China's oldest continuously inhabited urban centers — with documented history spanning more than 3,600 years — and today one of its most rapidly growing major cities.

Zhengzhou was the site of the ancient Shang dynasty capital Ao (c. 1600–1300 BCE), one of the earliest urban centers in Chinese history. Archaeological excavations have uncovered Shang-era palace foundations, bronze casting workshops, and oracle bone inscriptions at the Zhengzhou Shang City site. The city was the central node of Chinese civilization during the early Bronze Age — its Shang-era walls (3.2 km circumference) represent a major urban investment of the period.

Modern Zhengzhou's prominence is largely a product of the railway age — it stands at the intersection of China's north-south and east-west rail lines, making it one of China's most critical logistical hubs. The city's explosive growth in the 21st century has been driven by Foxconn's massive iPhone assembly complex (employing 300,000 workers at peak) and by its development as a hub city in China's central plains urbanization drive. The catastrophic 2021 flood, in which Zhengzhou's subway tunnels filled with water killing hundreds, exposed vulnerabilities in China's rapid urbanization model.
